name: Lightweight Test Case Manager
description: A web application that replaces Excel-based manual QA workflows for small teams. Full-stack: Node.js + Express backend, React 18 frontend, PostgreSQL database. Supports multi-user access with role-based permissions (admin / tester). QA writes test cases, runs test sessions, logs pass/fail/skip/blocked results with notes and attachments, and exports clean reports.
goals:
Replace Excel as the primary test case management tool for small QA teams
Reduce time to log and review a test run by 50% vs spreadsheet
Provide a shareable run report without manual formatting
Zero onboarding friction — usable within 5 minutes of install
outOfScope:
Jira CI/CD hooks or pipeline integration
Cloud sync or remote hosting
Environment and configuration management
Performance/load testing support
Dashboards, burndown charts, or trend analytics
Full-text Jira JQL search (deferred to v2.1)
Pushing test results back to Jira (deferred to v2.1)
stakeholders:
QA Engineer: Primary user — writes cases, executes runs, logs results
Admin: Manages users, projects, app configuration
PM: Reviews run reports and history
engineeringNotes:
All API routes prefixed /api/v1/
Auth: express-session + connect-pg-simple (session table in Postgres); bcrypt password hashing
Roles: admin (full access), tester (read all projects, write only assigned)
Data persisted in PostgreSQL via pg library
Numbered SQL migrations in /migrations tracked in schema_version table, run on startup
Steps stored as JSON array column on test_cases table
run_cases: all case fields copied at run creation (snapshot) — edits to cases do not affect historical runs
Error responses: { error: string, code: string } on all 4xx/5xx
NFR-01 (100ms) applies to all data API responses; PDF/CSV export endpoints are exempt
Jira API tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM per user; key stored in .env.local, never returned by any API
Jira global config stores base URL only (admin sets). Per-user email + API token stored in jira_user_credentials table.
Layout settings (app name, icon, favicon) stored in data/layout.json — not in DB
In production (npm start) Node serves client/dist on port 3000. In dev, Vite serves frontend on 5173, backend on 3000.
Docker: multi-stage Dockerfile (builder + runtime). docker-compose.yml includes postgres service with healthcheck and app service with persistent data volume.

techStack.frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React Query (@tanstack/react-query), @dnd-kit/core, Vite
techStack.backend: Node.js 20, Express 4, REST, Multer (file uploads), json2csv, cross-env, express-session, connect-pg-simple, bcrypt
techStack.database: PostgreSQL via pg library; AES-256-GCM for Jira token encryption
techStack.infrastructure: localhost or Docker. Single npm start command. Docker: multi-stage build, docker-compose with postgres service.
techStack.auth: express-session with Postgres session store; bcrypt (cost 12); roles: admin / tester
techStack.testing: Jest, Playwright (E2E), Supertest (API integration), MSW (frontend integration)
techStack.secrets: .env.local — JIRA_ENCRYPTION_KEY (auto-generated 32-byte hex), PostgreSQL connection config, SESSION_SECRET

globalNfrs.description: All data API responses must return within 100ms for datasets up to 500 test cases. PDF and CSV export endpoints are explicitly exempt.
All multi-step writes use PostgreSQL transactions with rollback on failure — DB must never be left in a corrupt state.
Core workflows (write case, run session, log result) must be fully keyboard-navigable with visible focus indicators.
App starts with npm start and is accessible at http://localhost:3000 within 10 seconds, including DB init and migration execution.
Run case results auto-saved with 500ms debounce after each status change or note input — no data loss if browser tab closed mid-run.
Jira API tokens encrypted using AES-256-GCM before storage in PostgreSQL. Encryption key stored in .env.local and never returned by any API response.
All Jira API calls proxied through backend. LTCM degrades gracefully if Jira is unreachable — local data always accessible, Jira-specific UI shows offline indicator.

activities.label: Authentication & Users
activities.description: Multi-user access with role-based permissions. Admin manages user accounts and project assignments. Per-user Jira credentials. Forced password change on first login.

screens.name: Change Password
screens.navigatesFrom: Forced on first login; Settings → change password

tasks.label: Login & Session
tasks.description: Users authenticate with username + password. Sessions persisted in Postgres. Forced password change on first login.

apiContracts.responses: 200: { id, username, role, mustChangePassword } | 401: invalid credentials

stories.title: As a user I can log in and maintain a session across browser reloads
stories.description:
AC: Unauthenticated users are redirected to /login
AC: Login form accepts username + password; shows error on wrong credentials
AC: Successful login redirects to the last visited page (or /)
AC: Session persists across page reloads for 7 days
AC: Logout clears session and redirects to /login
AC: On first login, user is redirected to /change-password before accessing any other page
AC: Admin account seeded automatically on first startup if no users exist
AC: GET /api/v1/auth/me returns current session user
stories.edgeCases:
Session cookie expired mid-session — next API call returns 401, frontend redirects to login
Admin changes own password — session remains active

tasks.label: User Management
tasks.description: Admin can create, deactivate, and reset passwords for tester accounts. Assign testers to projects at creation or via edit.

apiContracts.responses: 200: User[] — id, username, email, role, is_active

stories.title: As an admin I can create and manage tester accounts
stories.description:
AC: Settings → Users tab lists all users with role badge, email, active/inactive state
AC: Create User form: username (required), email (optional), role (tester/admin), initial password
AC: Deactivate/reactivate toggles is_active — inactive users cannot log in
AC: Reset password sets a new password (admin does not need current password)
AC: Admin cannot deactivate their own account
AC: Tester accounts can only read all projects but only write to assigned ones
stories.edgeCases:
Last active admin deactivated — prevented with error
Tester logs in and tries to edit unassigned project — 403 returned

stories.title: As an admin I can assign testers to projects
stories.description:
AC: Create Project and Edit Project modals include a Testers picker (checkbox list of active users)
AC: Selected testers are saved as project members
AC: Tester can see all projects but can only log results on projects they are assigned to
AC: Project member list accessible via GET /api/v1/projects/:id/members
stories.edgeCases:
Removing all testers from a project — allowed; project becomes admin-only
Deleting a user — removes them from all project member lists

activities.label: Infrastructure & Settings
activities.description: Foundation layer: PostgreSQL DB, numbered migrations, health check, backup/restore, DB config UI, server restart, offline detection, app customisation.

nfrs.description: All data API responses must return within 100ms for datasets up to 500 test cases. PDF and CSV export are exempt.
PostgreSQL writes that span multiple tables must use transactions with rollback on failure.
App starts with npm start and is accessible at http://localhost:3000 within 10 seconds, including DB init and migration execution.

tasks.label: DB Initialisation & Migrations
tasks.description: On startup, app connects to PostgreSQL, runs any pending numbered SQL migrations from /migrations in sequence, tracks applied migrations in schema_version table.

stories.title: As a QA I can start the app and have the DB schema created automatically
stories.description:
AC: App connects to PostgreSQL using config from .env.local or DB settings
AC: All pending /migrations/*.sql files are executed in numeric order on startup
AC: schema_version table tracks applied migrations — already-applied are skipped
AC: Console prints each migration applied or 'Schema up to date'
AC: GET /api/v1/health returns dbConnected: true when connected
stories.edgeCases:
DB unreachable on startup — app starts in disconnected mode, does not crash
Migration SQL is invalid — transaction rollback, error logged

tasks.label: Database Config UI
tasks.description: QA can configure PostgreSQL connection details from Settings → System. Supports test connection, save & reconnect, edit credentials.

stories.title: As a QA I can configure and test my PostgreSQL connection from Settings
stories.description:
AC: Settings → System tab shows current DB connection details (host, port, db name, user, password masked)
AC: Edit mode allows changing all fields
AC: Test Connection verifies credentials without saving
AC: Save & Connect saves and immediately reconnects the app
AC: Password field shows placeholder if already set
stories.edgeCases:
Saving invalid credentials — shows error, existing connection remains active
DB becomes unreachable after save — health polling detects and shows offline screen

tasks.label: DB Offline Detection
tasks.description: When DB is unreachable, the app shows a full-screen offline notice instead of project content, with a link to Settings → System.

stories.title: As a QA I see a clear offline screen when the database is not reachable
stories.description:
AC: Frontend polls GET /api/v1/health every 5 seconds
AC: When dbConnected is false, a full-screen 'Database not reachable' screen replaces all content (except Settings)
AC: Screen includes a 'Database settings' link that navigates to /settings?tab=system
AC: Settings page remains accessible so the QA can fix the connection
AC: When DB reconnects, the offline screen disappears automatically
stories.edgeCases: QA is mid-run when DB drops — offline screen appears, run state is preserved in DB once reconnected

tasks.label: Backup & Restore
tasks.description: QA can export all data as a JSON backup and restore from a previous backup.

stories.title: As a QA I can export and restore a full data backup
stories.description:
AC: Settings → System shows Export Backup and Import Backup buttons
AC: Export downloads a JSON file with all projects, suites, cases, runs, run_cases
AC: Import shows a confirm dialog warning that all existing data will be overwritten
AC: After successful restore the page reloads
AC: Invalid file formats are rejected with a clear error
stories.edgeCases: Restore file from a future schema version — rejected with SCHEMA_MISMATCH error

tasks.label: Server Restart API & Button
tasks.description: Backend exposes a restart endpoint. Settings → Utilities shows a Restart Server button.

stories.title: As a QA I can restart the backend server from the Settings UI
stories.description:
AC: Settings → Utilities shows a 'Restart Server' card with a button
AC: Clicking the button calls POST /api/v1/admin/restart
AC: Button shows spinner and 'Restarting…' while pending
AC: Page reloads automatically after 4 seconds
AC: Backend spawns a new node process via child_process.spawn and exits cleanly
stories.edgeCases: Server takes longer than 4s to restart — page reload may show brief error; user can manually refresh

tasks.label: Layout Settings
tasks.description: Admin can customise the app name, choose an icon from a preset library, and upload a favicon. Changes reflected on login page and browser tab.

apiContracts.responses: 200: { appName, iconName, hasFavicon } — public, no auth required

apiContracts.requestBody: multipart/form-data: { file } — max 1MB, image types only

stories.title: As an admin I can customise the app name, icon, and favicon
stories.description:
AC: Settings → Layout tab (admin only) shows app name input, icon picker grid, and favicon upload section
AC: Icon picker shows 17 preset Lucide icons as selectable squares with live preview
AC: Changing app name or icon updates the sidebar branding, login page heading, and browser tab title immediately
AC: Favicon upload accepts common image formats (PNG, ICO, SVG) up to 1MB; replaces existing favicon
AC: Favicon delete removes file and reverts to default browser behaviour
AC: GET /api/v1/settings/layout is public (no auth) so the login page can use branding before sign-in
AC: Settings stored in data/layout.json — not in the database
stories.edgeCases:
Favicon file too large — rejected with clear error, existing favicon unchanged
App name cleared — reverts to default 'LTCM'

activities.label: Project & Suite Management
activities.description: QA organises test cases into Projects (top-level containers) and Suites (feature/module groupings within a project). Includes display IDs, stats panels with All Time / Last Run toggle, and suite ordering.

screens.name: Suite Page
screens.navigatesFrom: Click suite card or nav suite row

tasks.label: Projects CRUD
tasks.description: QA can create, rename, and delete projects. Projects list shows last run status. Demo projects can only be deleted by admins.

apiContracts.responses: 204 | 409: active run exists | 403: demo project, admin required

stories.title: As a QA I can create, rename and delete projects
stories.description:
AC: Projects list shows all projects with name, description, last run status pill, Jira project key badge
AC: Create project modal: name (required, max 100 chars), optional description, optional Jira Project Key, optional tester assignment
AC: Edit project modal: same fields plus current tester list pre-loaded
AC: Inline rename on project page
AC: Delete blocked if an in-progress run exists — shows error
AC: Delete requires confirmation dialog
AC: Demo projects (is_demo = true) can only be deleted by admins — delete button hidden for testers
stories.edgeCases:
Duplicate project name — allowed (no uniqueness constraint at project level)
Delete last project — allowed, app shows empty state
Tester attempts to delete demo project — button not shown

tasks.label: Suites CRUD & Ordering
tasks.description: QA can create, rename, delete, and reorder suites within a project. Suites have TS-N display IDs.

stories.title: As a QA I can manage suites within a project
stories.description:
AC: Project overview shows suite cards with TS-N ID, name, case count, pass rate bar
AC: Create suite from project overview or suite page
AC: Inline rename by clicking the suite name in suite page header
AC: Delete suite with confirmation — cascades to all cases
AC: Suite sort order persisted; drag-to-reorder within project overview
AC: TS-N IDs shown in nav sidebar and suite headers
stories.edgeCases: Delete suite with cases linked to completed runs — allowed; run snapshots are preserved

tasks.label: All Time / Last Run Stats Toggle
tasks.description: Project overview and suite page each have a toggle to switch the stats panel between All Time aggregated results and the latest run (with live refresh for in-progress runs).

stories.title: As a QA I can toggle the project overview stats between All Time and Last Run
stories.description:
AC: Project overview stats panel has an 'All Time / Last Run' pill toggle in the top-right
AC: All Time view shows aggregated pass/fail/skip/blocked/na bar + counts across all runs
AC: Last Run view shows: status badge (Completed / In Progress), run number + name, date, View Report link, overall bar, and per-suite mini bars
AC: In-progress runs auto-refresh every 5 seconds in Last Run view
AC: Toggle selection persisted to localStorage per project (ltcm-proj-view-{projectId})
AC: Panel hidden if no runs exist
stories.edgeCases:
Run transitions from in-progress to completed while viewing — auto-refresh picks it up within 5s
No runs yet — stats panel not shown at all

stories.title: As a QA I can toggle the suite page stats between All Time and Last Run
stories.description:
AC: Suite page stats bar has an 'All Time / Last Run' pill toggle in the top-right
AC: All Time view shows aggregated pass/fail/skip/blocked/na bar and pass rate across all runs for that suite
AC: Last Run view shows: status badge, run number, date, View Report link, overall bar for suite cases, and per-case status list
AC: In-progress runs auto-refresh every 5 seconds
AC: Toggle selection persisted to localStorage per suite (ltcm-suite-view-{suiteId})
AC: Panel hidden if suite has no runs
stories.edgeCases:
Suite cases in the latest run filtered by suite_name match — only relevant cases shown
Suite not included in the latest run — shows run header with 0 cases

activities.label: Test Case Authoring
activities.description: QA writes, edits, duplicates, moves, reorders, and imports test cases. Cases have TC-N display IDs, steps, priority, preconditions, tags, and full execution history. Jira issue keys can be linked with or without Jira configured.

screens.name: New / Edit Test Case
screens.navigatesFrom: Suite page → New Case or Edit button

screens.name: Case Detail Pane
screens.navigatesFrom: Click case row in suite page

tasks.label: Test Case CRUD
tasks.description: QA can create, edit, delete, duplicate, and move test cases between suites.

apiContracts.responses: 200: TestCase[] with case_number, last_run_status, last_run_id, last_run_number

apiContracts.requestBody: { title, steps[], expected_result, preconditions?, priority?, tags? }
{ title?, steps?, expected_result?, preconditions?, priority?, order?, tags? }

apiContracts.responses: 200: CaseHistoryEntry[] — all runs containing this case, ordered newest first

stories.title: As a QA I can write and manage test cases with steps and expected results
stories.description:
AC: New Case form has: Suite selector, Title (required, max 100 chars), Preconditions (optional), Steps (at least 1 required, Enter to add new, Backspace on empty to remove), Expected Result (required), Priority (high/medium/low, default medium), Tags (optional, comma/space/Enter to add)
AC: Add Step button appears below the steps list
AC: TC-N display ID assigned automatically (globally sequential)
AC: Edit form pre-fills all fields
AC: Duplicate creates a copy with 'Copy of' prefix in same suite
AC: Move shows other suites in a dropdown; case moves immediately
AC: Drag-to-reorder within suite, order persisted
stories.edgeCases:
Title > 100 chars — UI enforces max, backend validates
Steps array empty on submit — validation error

stories.title: As a QA I can see the last run result and full run history for a case
stories.description:
AC: Case list rows show a clickable status pill (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/BLOCKED/NA) for the last run
AC: Clicking the pill navigates to the run summary
AC: Case detail pane shows a 'Run History' section listing all runs, each with status pill, run number, and date
AC: Clicking a history entry navigates to that run summary
AC: History ordered newest first
stories.edgeCases: Case never run — no pill shown, history section hidden

tasks.label: Excel Import
tasks.description: QA can bulk-import test cases from an Excel file. A template is available for download.

stories.title: As a QA I can bulk-import test cases from Excel
stories.description:
AC: Suite page header shows an Import button
AC: Import accepts .xlsx files with columns: Title, Preconditions, Steps (newline-separated), Expected Result, Priority
AC: Rows with missing Title or Expected Result are skipped with an error note
AC: Import result summary shows imported count, skipped count, and per-row errors
AC: Template download available from Settings → Utilities
stories.edgeCases:
File is not a valid .xlsx — rejected with clear error
All rows invalid — 0 imported, all errors listed

activities.label: Test Run Execution
activities.description: QA starts a run, steps through each case marking Pass/Fail/Skip/Blocked/NA with notes and attachments, creates or links Jira bugs, and completes, cancels, or clones the run.

nfrs.description: Run case results must be auto-saved (debounce 500ms) after each status change or note input — no data loss if browser tab is closed mid-run.

tasks.label: Start & Execute a Run
tasks.description: QA starts a run, optionally selecting specific suites and environment. Cases are snapshotted. QA steps through marking results.

apiContracts.responses: 201: Run | 409: in-progress run exists | 400: no cases
200: RunCase[] — snapshot with status, note, step_results, case_number

stories.title: As a QA I can start and execute a test run
stories.description:
AC: Start Run modal shows run name (optional), suite selector (default all), environment (optional), Jira Fix Version (optional if Jira connected)
AC: Only one in-progress run allowed per project
AC: Cases are snapshotted at run creation — later edits to cases don't affect the run
AC: Execute screen shows case list on left, case detail + verdict on right
AC: Status buttons: Pass, Fail, Skip, Blocked, Not Applicable
AC: Notes textarea auto-saves with 500ms debounce
AC: Step-level pass/fail with actual result input
AC: RUN-N and TC-N display IDs shown throughout
stories.edgeCases:
Suite has 0 cases — blocked from starting (backend returns 400)
Browser closed mid-run — results preserved on reload

tasks.label: Attachments on Results
tasks.description: QA can attach files (screenshots, logs) to individual run case results during execution.

stories.title: As a QA I can attach files to a run case result
stories.description:
AC: Below the notes field in the execute screen, an 'Attachments' section shows an Attach button
AC: Clicking Attach opens a file picker (any file type, max 20MB)
AC: Attached files appear as a list with name, size, download and delete buttons
AC: Files stored on disk in data/attachments/; metadata in run_case_attachments table
AC: Deleting an attachment removes both DB row and file from disk
AC: Attachments cascade-delete when run case is deleted
stories.edgeCases:
File > 20MB — rejected with clear error
Server disk full — upload fails gracefully with error message

tasks.label: Complete, Cancel & Clone Runs
tasks.description: QA can complete a run (locking results), cancel a run (discarding it), or clone a run (fresh copy with same cases).

stories.title: As a QA I can complete, cancel, or clone a run
stories.description:
AC: Execute header shows 'Cancel Run' (secondary, red hover) and 'Complete Run' (primary) buttons
AC: Complete Run with unmarked cases prompts to force-skip remaining
AC: Cancel Run requires confirmation — marks run as 'cancelled', restores project status to last completed run
AC: Clone Run (from summary page) creates a new in-progress run with the same case snapshot and fresh statuses
AC: Clone Run name defaults to 'Clone of {original name}'
AC: Clone blocked if an in-progress run already exists
stories.edgeCases: Completing run while another tab has it open — second tab shows 'Run completed' state on next poll

stories.title: As a QA I can re-run only the failed/blocked/skipped cases from a completed run
stories.description:
AC: Run summary shows 'Re-run Failures' button when failed, blocked, or skipped cases exist
AC: Clicking creates a new run containing only those cases (default: fail + blocked + skip)
AC: New run navigates directly to execute screen
AC: If an in-progress run already exists, shows error toast
stories.edgeCases: All cases passed — Re-run Failures button not shown

activities.label: Run History & Reporting
activities.description: QA and PM review past runs, view pass/fail/skip/blocked summaries, see a vs-last-run diff, and export clean PDF or CSV reports.

tasks.label: Run Summary & Diff
tasks.description: After completing a run, QA sees pass/fail/skip/blocked/na stats, a progress bar, per-case results, and a diff vs the previous run.

apiContracts.responses: 200: RunSummary { passed, failed, skipped, blocked, na, total, duration_ms, diff: { regressions, fixes, newCases }, defects[], cases[] }

stories.title: As a QA I can review a completed run with stats and a vs-last-run diff
stories.description:
AC: Summary shows RUN-N heading, completion date/time, duration, environment, Jira version
AC: Stats grid: Passed (green), Failed (red), Skipped (yellow), Blocked (orange), N/A (grey)
AC: Pass rate calculated excluding Blocked and N/A
AC: Progress bar shows proportional results
AC: Diff section: Regressions (was passing, now failing), Fixes (was failing, now passing), New Cases
AC: Cases table sorted: fail → blocked → pass → skip → na
AC: TC-N shown per case
stories.edgeCases:
First run — no diff shown
All cases N/A — pass rate shows 0% with note

tasks.label: Export CSV & PDF
tasks.description: QA can export run results as CSV or HTML (print-to-PDF) from the run summary.

apiContracts.responses: 200: text/csv with ID, Title, Suite, Status, Note columns

stories.title: As a QA I can export run results as CSV or PDF
stories.description:
AC: Run summary shows CSV and PDF export buttons
AC: CSV includes columns: ID (TC-N), Title, Suite, Priority, Status, Note
AC: PDF opens a print-ready HTML page in a new tab
AC: Both include run name, date, environment, stats summary in header
AC: Export endpoints exempt from 100ms NFR
stories.edgeCases: Run with 0 cases — export produces header-only file

activities.label: Jira Integration
activities.description: QA connects LTCM to Jira Cloud, links test cases to issue keys (with or without Jira configured), creates defects with attachments, updates existing bugs, and associates runs with Fix Versions. Global config stores base URL only; each user manages their own credentials.

nfrs.description: Jira API tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM before storage. Key in .env.local, never returned by API.
LTCM degrades gracefully if Jira is unreachable — local data always accessible, Jira UI shows offline indicator.

tasks.label: Jira Connection Config
tasks.description: Admin sets the global Jira base URL. Each user saves their own email and API token (encrypted). Jira project key is per-project.

stories.title: As a QA I can connect LTCM to Jira Cloud with per-user encrypted credentials
stories.description:
AC: Settings → Jira tab has two sections: Admin (base URL, admin only) and My Credentials (email + API token, per user)
AC: Admin saves the global Jira base URL
AC: Each user saves their own email and API token; token encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before writing to DB
AC: Connected state shows base URL and credential email — token never displayed
AC: Test Connection verifies and shows Jira display name using current user's credentials
AC: Jira project key is set per-project (in Create/Edit Project modal)
AC: Disconnect (admin) removes base URL; existing case links and run version refs preserved
stories.edgeCases:
Jira unreachable during test — 502 with JIRA_UNREACHABLE code
User has no credentials but global config set — can still save issue keys (no summary enrichment)

tasks.label: Link Cases to Jira Issues
tasks.description: QA can link/unlink test cases to Jira issue keys at any time — Jira connection is not required to save a key. When Jira is connected, links are enriched with issue summary and URL.

apiContracts.responses: 200: JiraLink[] — { id, case_id, jira_issue_key, jira_issue_summary, jira_issue_url, created_at }
201: JiraLink | 404: issue not found in Jira (only when Jira configured) | 409: already linked

stories.title: As a QA I can link a test case to one or more Jira issue keys
stories.description:
AC: Case editor sidebar always shows a 'Linked Issues' section — visible regardless of Jira connection
AC: Input accepts one or more keys (comma or space separated, e.g. PROJ-1, PROJ-2)
AC: For existing cases: keys are linked immediately on Enter or click
AC: For new (unsaved) cases: keys stored as pending — linked on save, discarded if not saved
AC: When Jira is configured and user has credentials: issue summary and URL fetched and stored
AC: When Jira not configured: key saved with null summary/URL; note shown explaining enrichment requires Jira setup
AC: When Jira unreachable: key saved without enrichment (NFR-08 graceful degradation)
AC: Linked issue keys shown as chips; clickable to open in Jira if URL available
AC: Remove button unlinks the issue
AC: Case list rows and detail pane show linked issue keys
stories.edgeCases:
Issue key doesn't exist in Jira (when Jira configured) — 404 error shown, link not saved
Invalid key format (not PROJ-123 pattern) — rejected with validation error

tasks.label: Create Defect & Update Existing Bug
tasks.description: When a case fails or is blocked, QA can create a new Jira bug (with attachments) or update an existing bug (post comment + link). Two distinct buttons shown.

apiContracts.responses: 200: { ok, issueKey, issueUrl } — also saves to case_jira_links

AC: 'Update Existing Bug' button (orange) expands an inline input for the issue key

AC: Issue key is saved to case_jira_links and shown in the existing links section
AC: Issue summary fetched from Jira and stored with the link
